title: Hearing Bolden at Lincoln Park and the parks
summary: Bolden at Lincoln Park and elsewhere, his dominance when he played against other bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Can you remember any more about Bowden? Where did you hear him? Aside from Globe Hall, did you ever go out to Lincoln Park?

Lincoln Park. I went to all the park. Jonathan Park. He was all over. I used to like him. He was playing the most of the other corners. He was playing the most of the corners of the world. Nothing in the city. And every way he would play, he could have the best corner, the best corner player. Supposed to be. Yeah. When he played against some other fellas, he'd have the crowd. But when all the little house cover would get out there and start the showin' out, he'd never sit down. He'd stand up all the time.

Where'd he go? It's just a man for us to be skint. It happened with that little boy. You know I used to, they were on La Perouse and Pril. And he was out the background. He could hear him just like I thought he was right there. Sometimes I didn't feel like going out. I'd sit down at the corner. He'd get old Bolden, show him out of every number. He'd kill them all. All of them. Man used to play for the strong too, because I don't like Bolden.
